title: Cursor resilience, idempotent iterator, and HTTP error taxonomy for vector endpoints
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Multiple clients (legacy SDKs and third-party integrations) observe inconsistent behaviour across the embeddings and rerank iterator endpoints: cursor invalidation under partial stream delivery, non-idempotent cursor creation, and varied HTTP error codes for the same underlying server conditions. This causes retries to either be unsafe or unnecessary and complicates client SDK logic. Goal: Provide a compatibility layer and concrete server-side behaviour that guarantees (1) cursor creation and advancement are idempotent from a client perspective, (2) cursors tolerate partial acknowledgement and transient worker restarts (cursor resilience), and (3) server error responses are normalized into a clear HTTP status + retry-hint surface that legacy clients can handle predictably.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Existing SDKs can paginate embeddings/rerank results without schema changes and without increased 500s after compatibility layer is enabled
2) Cursor tokens are stable for a given iterator state; re-submitting the same cursor+params must be safe and return the same next page or a clear terminal response

3) Define and publish HTTP error mapping doc that maps internal error classes to these surface codes: 200, 400, 401, 403, 404, 409 (conflict), 429 (rate limit), 500 (internal), 503 (unavailable) along with Retry-After and Retry-After-Hint semantics

4) Provide a server-side fallback: when a requested cursor is missing due to GC/eviction, return 409 with body providing a small resume token that client libraries can use for best-effort reconstruction
5) Add automated integration tests covering worker restart during active long-running iterators and ensure no duplicate page delivery beyond consumer-ack semantics
6) Rollout flag to enable compatibility layer per-region and per-customer tier with no SLA regressions during canary.
7) Documentation and migration guide published in Confluence and linked from API changelog before GA.
implementation_notes: Introduce a thin compatibility façade in the iterator gateway that canonicalizes incoming pagination params and cursor envelopes from legacy clients

Store a lightweight cursor manifest keyed by cursor-id + client-hash containing: sequence pointer, checksum of query params, creation_ts, and a low-size resume snapshot used to rebuild the iterator state after eviction
Cursor manifest lifetime: implement configurable retention policy with default 48h, and a tombstone window of 2h to allow safe replays
Map internal errors to surface codes in a central error-mapper module. Add 'X-RI-Retry-Hint' header that can be one of ["none", "fast-retry", "backoff", "recreate-cursor"]
Idempotency: use client-provided idempotency-key when present; otherwise normalize request body to a canonical fingerprint to detect retries and return cached result when safe
Edge-case: when stream partials are delivered and KV cache lost mid-iterator, the gateway should emit 409 with resume token rather than 500.
rollout_plan: 1) Implement compatibility façade behind feature flag (gateway.compat.iterator_compat) and add unit + integration tests
2) Internal canary: enable flag for infra team + 3 internal customers for 48h, monitor error rates and duplicate events
3) Gradual regional rollout: 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 7 days with automated rollback on error budgets
4) Coordinate with SDK teams to release minor client versions that respect the new Retry-Hint header and resume-token flow
5) Post-rollout: remove legacy branch code after 6 months when usage of legacy cursor envelopes < 5% (tracked via telemetry).
monitoring: Dashboards: cursor_create_rate, cursor_recreate_rate, resume_token_issued, iterator_duplicate_pages, iterator_error_rate_by_status
SLOs: iterator_success_rate >= 99.5% over 7d during canary; duplicate-page-rate < 0.1%
Alerting: page_duplications > 0.5% in 1h -> P1 on-call; 5xx spike post-rollout -> automatic feature-flag rollback
Add log fields: cursor_manifest_hits, cursor_manifest_misses, retry_hint, resume_token_id
